rationale: C07 is the clear drafting parent. The child expressly identifies the September 27, 1952 proclamation as arising from the same September 25, 1952 Tariff Commission report and as having carried out part of its recommendations. It then uses C07's sequence and highly specific language—section 22 investigation of tree nuts, the 1952–53 crop-year finding, protection of an Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act program, and a finding that an import restriction is necessary—while adapting the remedy from almond fees to a filbert quota. C19 supplies a closely related earlier tree-nut formulation, and C03 uses nearly identical section 22 machinery, but neither is as direct as C07.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the President caused the United States Tariff Commission to make an investigation to determine whether almonds, filberts, walnuts, Brazil nuts, or cashews are being or are practically certain to be imported ... as to render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, certain programs or operations undertaken by the Department of Agriculture
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I caused the United States Tariff Commission to make an investigation to determine whether certain tree nuts are being or are practically certain to be imported ... as to render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, certain programs or operations undertaken by the Department of Agriculture
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive shared description of the same section 22 tree-nut investigation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the said Commission reported to the President on September 25, 1952 ... and the President ... issued a proclamation on September 27, 1952 ... carrying out in part the said recommendations
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Commission reported to me on September 25, 1952 its findings resulting from such investigation
shared_material.explanation: The child expressly incorporates C07's report and identifies C07 as the earlier partial implementation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: shelled filberts ... are practically certain to be imported during the remainder of the 12-month period ending September 30, 1953 ... as to render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, the program undertaken by the Department of Agriculture with respect to filberts pursuant to the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, as amended
shared_material.parent_excerpt: shelled almonds ... are practically certain to be imported ... during the period October 1, 1952 to September 30, 1953 ... as to render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with the program undertaken by the Department of Agriculture with respect to almonds pursuant to the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, as amended
shared_material.explanation: The later finding closely tracks C07 while substituting filberts for almonds and narrowing the applicable portion of the same crop year.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the imposition of the quantitative limitation hereinafter proclaimed is shown by the investigation ... to be necessary in order that the entry of imported shelled filberts ... will not render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, the said program
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the imposition of the fees hereinafter proclaimed are shown by such investigation ... to be necessary in order that the entry of imported shelled almonds ... will not render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, the said program
shared_material.explanation: Concrete operative bridge language is reused with the remedy and commodity adapted.
